text: When designing a REST API, following best practices ensures it is easy to use and maintain. First, use clear and consistent endpoints, such as `/users` or `/orders`, to represent resources. Always return appropriate HTTP status codes, like `200` for success and `404` for not found. Good documentation is essential; it should explain each endpoint, its parameters, and expected responses. Finally, implement versioning, for example by adding `/v1/` to the URL, so that changes do not break existing clients. These practices make your API reliable and developer-friendly.
